review_notes:
I read all four declarations in SphereVolume.lean: `sphereCone_injOn`, `sphereCone_image`, `sphere_toSphere_local` and `sphere_induced_volume`. I also read the definitions they depend on in SphereConeChart.lean (`sphereParam`, `sphereParam_norm`, `sphereCone`, `sphereConeDeriv`, `sphereCone_det`), `chartPreimage` and `lintegral_join_product` (SphereConeMeasure.lean), and grepped for uses of these lemmas.

The setting is fixed on purpose: the unit 2-sphere `Sphere` in `E3`, with charts `extChartAt I2 p` and `sphereMetric`. The main theorem says the Riemannian volume of the sphere metric equals Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere`. Proving it for spheres of other dimensions would need substantial new mathematics: a cone map and determinant computation for n-spheres, plus a density computation in place of `sphereParamDeriv_density`. That is outside this rubric.

I checked two smaller generalisations of the helper lemmas:
1. `sphereCone_injOn` only uses positivity of the radii (`hr.1`, `ht.1`, through `abs_of_pos` and `ne_of_gt`). So it would also hold for `Ioi 0`, or for any set of radii contained in `Ioi 0`.
2. `sphereCone_image` would hold for any set of radii `T`, giving `T • (Subtype.val '' …)`.

Both are valid, but I don't count them as useful generalisations. Each lemma is used exactly once, inside `sphere_toSphere_local`. There, the interval `Ioo 0 1` is forced by the definition of `Measure.toSphere` (the `toSphere_apply'` rewrite) and by `lintegral_join_product`, which itself takes `Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1` as given. No other code in the sources uses these lemmas with other radius sets. So the change would be abstraction without a demonstrated user benefit, which the rubric says not to demand. `sphere_toSphere_local` and `sphere_induced_volume` already state their results for any measurable set and any base point, with no extra restrictive assumptions.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not search every downstream file for possible future uses of a more general cone-image lemma.
